title: Slav Defense: Exchange Variation
line: White trades pawns at once, and both sides have the same pawns.

steps.text: The Slav Defense, and White trades pawns on d5 at once.
Take back with the pawn on c6. Both sides now have the same pawns, and the c-file is open.
Bring the knight out to guard the center pawn.
Bring the other knight out. It watches the center squares too.
Bring the bishop out before you move the king pawn.
Move the pawn in front of your king one square to free your other bishop.
steps.after: White's queen attacks your pawn on b7, which your bishop left behind.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out to pin the knight on c3. It also stands in the queen's path to the pawn on b7.

wrong.c6a5: The queen steps aside with check from a4. Black must answer the check, and the knight on the edge does little.

steps.after: The pawn on b7 is safe, and the knight on c3 is pinned. Both sides have the same pawns and active pieces.

summary: The pawns are the same, so the side with more active pieces does better. Watch the pawn the bishop leaves behind.
